ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
By connecting a force sensor to a computer, rapidly changing forces can be measured. In Figure 1, point $O$ is the fixed suspension point of a simple pendulum. The small pendulum bob (which can be considered a point mass) is pulled to point $A$, where the string is taut. When the bob is released, it swings back and forth between points $A$, $B$, and $C$ in the vertical plane, where point $B$ is the lowest position in the motion, and $\angle A O B{=}\angle C O B{=}\theta$, with $\theta$ being less than $5^{\circ}$ and unknown. Figure 2 shows the curve of the tension force $F$ in the string as a function of time $t$, obtained from the computer, where $t=0$ corresponds to the moment when the bob starts moving from point $A$. It is given that $g$ is $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the vibration period and length of a simple pendulum?
2. What is the mass of the pendulum bob?
3. What is the maximum speed during the motion of the pendulum ball?

Figure 2 shows the curve of the tension force $F$ in the string as a function of time $t$, obtained from the computer, where $t=0$ corresponds to the moment when the bob starts moving from point $A$. It is given that $g$ is $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. 1. What is the vibration period and length of a simple pendulum? 2. What is the mass of the pendulum bob? 3. What is the maximum speed during the motion of the pendulum ball?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the images: In Figure 1, the pendulum string is suspended from fixed point O, the lowest position is B, the right endpoint is A, the left endpoint is C, OB is the vertical direction, and the angles between OA, OC and OB are both marked as θ. Figure 2 is the curve of tension F with time t; the vertical axis is marked with two dashed lines 0.495 N and 0.510 N; the curve is at the smaller value 0.495 N at t=0, and reaches the smaller value again at positions such as t=0.2π s, 0.4π s, and the maximum value reaches 0.510 N. Then reason: t=0 is the moment when the small ball is released from rest at point A. At the two endpoints A and C, the velocity is 0 and the tension in the rope is the smallest, so two adjacent minimum tension values in the figure correspond to motion from one endpoint to the other endpoint, and the time interval is half a period. From the figure, the interval between adjacent minimum values is read as 0.2π s, therefore T/2=0.2π s, obtaining the swing period T=0.4π s. The small-angle simple pendulum period formula is T=2π√(L/g). Substitute g=10 m/s² and T=0.4π s: L=g(T/2π)^2=10×(0.4π/2π)^2=10×0.2^2=0.40 m. At endpoint A or C, the velocity is 0, and the radial equation gives F_min=mg cosθ=0.495 N. At the lowest point B, the velocity is maximum, F_max=mg+mv_max²/L; by conservation of mechanical energy v_max²=2gL(1−cosθ), so F_max=mg+2mg(1−cosθ)=mg(3−2cosθ)=0.510 N. Taking F_max+2F_min=3mg, get mg=(0.510+2×0.495)/3=0.500 N, therefore m=0.500/10=0.050 kg. Also from F_min=mg cosθ, cosθ=0.495/0.500=0.99. The maximum velocity v_max=√[2gL(1−cosθ)]=√[2×10×0.40×(1−0.99)]=√0.08≈0.283 m/s.
